$comment: Machine-readable rights ledger for the rules-engine direction in issue #200. One entry per referenced game, recording what its license actually permits for a NooPunk rulebook released under the chosen Creative Commons license. LICENSE FINDINGS ONLY: nothing here asserts that any third-party expression has been imported, and 'imported_expression' is false throughout. NooPunk is an unofficial independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher named here.
$retrieved_convention: Dates here are real-world metadata dates, NOT in-world canon dates (AGENTS.md section 6 limits in-world future dates to 20XX; this file makes no in-world claims).

target_license.rationale: CC BY-SA 4.0 is the only option that keeps BOTH compatible adaptation pathways open: it accepts CC BY 3.0 and CC BY-SA 3.0 material as compatible, so the Fate Core SRD (CC BY 3.0) and The Veil (CC BY-SA 3.0) can be adapted with attribution. Choosing CC BY 4.0 instead would forfeit the CC BY-SA pathway and forbid adapting The Veil's expression. Reciprocity is acceptable here because NooPunk wants to be reusable itself.
target_license.$not_applied: No LICENSE file is added by this record. Relicensing the repository is a one-way legal act for the author, not an agent.

decision_vocabulary.importable-cc: Expression may be adapted into a CC BY-SA 4.0 NooPunk release, with the attribution the source requires.
decision_vocabulary.principles-only: Design ideas/procedures may be independently implemented; the source's protected EXPRESSION may not be copied.
decision_vocabulary.no-reuse: Neither expression nor a derived table may be reproduced; the concept must be implemented from scratch if used at all.

compatibility_rule.statement: An entry may be marked importable-cc only when its license permits commercial reuse AND is compatible with CC BY-SA 4.0.
compatibility_rule.$why: A NonCommercial term cannot enter a commercially reusable CC BY/BY-SA release, and OGL Open Game Content cannot be relabelled as Creative Commons. Small edits do not change either fact.

sources.name: Fate Core System / Fate Accelerated Edition SRD
sources.role_in_noopunk: Narrativist centre — aspects, consequences, compels, fate points, scene-level stakes.
sources.verified: publisher site (fate-srd.com licensing page) plus the attribution bloc carried at the top of each SRD file
sources.notes: Evil Hat calls it 'the most liberal one possible' and states it is NOT viral. Compatibility with CC BY-SA 4.0 is one-way: the CC BY text may be adapted into a BY-SA work with attribution; the reverse is not implied.

sources.name: The Veil / The Veil: Cascade
sources.role_in_noopunk: Narrativist corner — fiction-first stakes, hard choices, social and emotional consequences.
sources.verified: the work's own license statement ('The text of The Veil: Cascade is licensed under the Creative Commons Share-alike 3.0 Unported (CC BY-SA 3.0)'), found in two independent copies; the publisher's own site was not fetched in this pass
sources.notes: Its own text records that some moves are 'tweaked or lifted straight from Apocalypse World ... used with his permission'. That permission was granted to THAT project and does not transfer to NooPunk: the AW-derived portions inside The Veil are not covered by The Veil's license. Do not copy those. CC BY-SA 3.0 is compatible with CC BY-SA 4.0 in the adaptation pathway, which is the concrete reason the recommended target is BY-SA and not BY.

sources.name: Cities Without Number System Reference Document
sources.role_in_noopunk: Gamist corner — fast procedures, generators, mission structure, encounter pacing.
sources.verified: the publisher's own storefront listing: 'provided under a Creative Commons 0 waiver allowing downloaders to copy, modify, reproduce, or otherwise use it for both personal and commercial purposes. Later versions of this file may be released, but any released version may be used'
sources.notes: CC0 is maximally compatible: no attribution obligation, no ShareAlike. CRITICAL SCOPE: the waiver covers the SRD, NOT the full commercial book. 'The full SRD, but not all parts of the original book.' Use only the SRD.

sources.name: Stars Without Number (Revised) SRD
sources.license: CC0 1.0 indicated, NOT verified at the publisher in this pass
sources.verified: NOT VERIFIED. Third-party reports (community discussion) and the publisher's sibling listings for CWN and Worlds Without Number both describe a Creative Commons 0 waiver, but the SWN SRD's own publisher listing was not located in this pass.
sources.notes: Downgraded to principles-only precisely because the issue forbids treating 'user reports CC' as a finding. Promote to importable-cc only after reading the SWN SRD's own license page.

sources.name: Fudge System Reference Document
sources.role_in_noopunk: Centre — the Attribute/Skill distinction and flexible trait-ladder adjudication.
sources.license: Open Game License 1.0a (designated Open Game Content)
sources.verified: publisher site, which states the SRD is released under the OGL, that Appendix I carries OGL 1.0a, and lists the three compliance obligations (include the license, update Section 15, designate OGC vs Product Identity)
sources.notes: OGL is not Creative Commons and OGC cannot be relabelled CC. Fudge's Attribute/Skill split and trait ladder are PROCEDURES and may be independently implemented; the SRD's wording and tables may not enter a CC-only rulebook without separate written permission.

sources.name: Fudge (1995 core rules) PDF
sources.license: special restrictive free-distribution license; NOT a CC grant
sources.verified: publisher's legalities page distinguishes the OGL-released SRD from the 1995 core, which carries its own limited license

sources.name: Psi-Punk SRD
sources.role_in_noopunk: Centre — the demonstration that psychic, cyber and astral subsystems can be built around a Fudge-style split.
sources.license: Open Game License 1.0a with declared Product Identity
sources.verified: the SRD's OGL legal page names the reserved material ('All content in the game's Introduction and in Chapter 1: The World of Psi-punk are considered Product Identity. Brain.Net, the sample adventure, is likewise ...'), and the publisher's announcement describes the SRD as the rules text with 'virtually none of the setting or fluff'
sources.notes: Two separate exclusions apply: OGL OGC cannot be relicensed CC, and the Product Identity sections are not open at all. Its structural lessons are implementable; its tables are not.

sources.name: Eclipse Phase, Second Edition
sources.role_in_noopunk: Simulationist corner — cyberware, networks, AI, PSI, transhumanism, equipment, tactical conflict.
sources.notes: The NonCommercial term is decisive: EP expression cannot enter a commercially reusable CC release. Causal modelling inspired by EP must be written independently.

sources.name: Transhumanity's Fate
sources.role_in_noopunk: Centre — a worked demonstration of a transhuman setting expressed in Fate.
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (per the issue's classification; not independently re-verified in this pass)
sources.verified: taken from the issue's own classification; the material is not present on disk and its own license page was not fetched

sources.name: Apocalypse World
sources.publisher: Lumpley Games (D. Vincent Baker & Meguey Baker)
sources.role_in_noopunk: Narrativist corner — GM moves, narrative clocks, fiction-first resolution.
sources.license: no Creative Commons grant; 'all rights reserved' with a per-request permission policy for words
sources.verified: the publisher's PbtA policy page: 'If you're using our words, you need our permission, per copyright law. If you aren't using our words, you don't need our permission'; the 2010 core text carries an all-rights-reserved notice
sources.notes: 'PbtA' is a descriptive design lineage, not a license grant. NooPunk may call itself PbtA-inspired when accurate, and must not describe itself as affiliated or licensed.
